Maya (devex): quick report from a customer call: their Go sample app hangs on generator streaming when user navigates away. They followed our example but it used context.Background().
Jon P: that will leak. Do we have a guidance snippet for http handlers?
Maya (devex): they used this pattern:
```go
stream, _ := client.Generator.Stream(context.Background(), req)
for stream.Next() { io.WriteString(w, stream.Token()) }
```
When client closes, server goroutine doesn't unblock.
Wei Z: fix is obvious: use the request context. Also Stream should be cancellable.
Jon P: API suggestion: Stream(ctx, req) should tie ctx to the internal http.Request. The returned Stream should expose Close() to cancel and close body. Next() should unstick when ctx.Done() fires.
Maya (devex): also docs: sample should show `defer stream.Close()` and a helper like `streamhttp.CopyToResponse(ctx, stream, w)` that watches r.Context().
Wei Z: added unit tests idea: use net.Pipe to simulate a server that blocks and assert Close() unblocks Next() quickly. Also test double Close() is safe.
build-bot: CI task created for PR draft (#3507).
Maya (devex): I'll open a small PR updating examples and adding Stream.Close() wrapper. Keeping retry behavior unchanged; we'll open separate RFC for resume semantics.
Jon P: cool. Make sure godoc notes Token() only valid immediately after Next() returns true.
Wei Z: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/3507. CI running.
build-bot: CI passed for #3507.
Maya (devex): merged. Added changelog blurb: "Call defer stream.Close() to ensure generator streams are cancelled on client disconnect."
Jon P: thanks. This should reduce onboarding friction.
